description: One call for the inner loop: the program read (whether it reads, the reader's diagnostics with their lines and codes, its measures and smells); where the reader refuses it, the mechanical fixes the engine would make on the flagged lines and what needs a person; and given what it must do (`intent`, or a `task` with cases and constraints), each case run and graded passed, failed or unchecked by the strongest layer the engine has for its intent, with the verdict, its layer and that layer's limits, each constraint measured, what went wrong and where to look. `next` says what to do next. Nothing is sealed: when every case passes, grade_quantum_program seals the grade. Never call a program correct past what its verdict's level and layer say. Each case's intent is held to the service's bounds before it runs, and a case past them is refused with the local command (`wai-quantum check`).

inputs.description: A generator's integer inputs, as {"n": 5}: the program's one case when the task gives no cases.

intent.description: What the program must do, as run_quantum_circuit takes it: one intent or a list (wai-quantum://docs/verdicts). Give this or `task`.

qasm.description: The program, OpenQASM 3 or 2, or a generator (integer input) with its values in `inputs` or in the task's cases.

seed.description: With intent: the sampling seed (1 when not given).

shots.description: With intent: the shots each run samples (16 when not given; an intent is decided on the program, not on these).

task.description: What the program must do, in the exercise form, as grade_quantum_program takes it: `intent` or `cases` (each {"name", "inputs", "intent"}), `job` ({"shots", "seed", "noise"}) and `constraints`.

name: check_quantum_program

anyOf.description: A program checked against what it must do (check_quantum_program on either MCP server, wai-quantum check, POST /v1/check, and the Python and npm packages' check): whether it reads, what the reader said, its measures and smells, the fixes the engine would make where it does not read, and given an intent or a task, its grade unsealed (wai.quantum.grade/1: each case passed, failed or unchecked with the verdict and layer that decided it, each constraint measured, what went wrong and where to look); the verdict, whether it passes, and the next thing to do. Nothing is sealed.

A grade's result (engine::grade, the provider protocol's section 8.10): a program held to a task's cases, sealed as a job so that anyone can run it again. Its request is {"grade": {"task": a task in the exercise form (exercise.v1.json) with no solution and no known wrong answers, "program": the OpenQASM text}}. The result gives each case's grade (passed, failed or unchecked) with the verdict that decided it and that verdict's layer, each constraint measured, what went wrong with where to look, whether the program passes, and one verdict of every case's checks, which a verifier works out again. The grade's receipt seals the task, the program and the grade together.

cases.description: Each case in the task's order: its name and inputs as the task gives them, its grade, and the verdict of its run with its intent, with that verdict's level, holds and layer beside it.

grade.description: passed: its intents hold, checked as proof or as evidence; failed: one does not hold, or the reader refused the program at the case's inputs; unchecked: neither was decided (no layer reached it, or the run was refused).

verdict.description: How far the engine checked an answer, as one level of an ordered ladder (wai-quantum://docs/verdicts): refused, parsed, executed, evidence, proof; and the layer that decided it, with that layer's limits. A level says how far the engine checked, not that the answer is good: holds says whether the intents held (true, false, or null when none was decided), and layer names what decided them: exact simulation, a stabilizer check, checked rewrites, the answer held to its problem's own checks, agreement of the run's samples with a simulation, samples held to a distribution, physical consistency, random states, or unchecked. A job's result carries one under verdict when the job gives an intent or asks for one, and the receipt seals it; both MCP servers state one beside every answer about a program.

pointer.description: Where to look first, in words; never the solution.

receipt.description: A result's receipt: an Ed25519 signature, by the key it names, over digest = BLAKE3("wai:quantum-service-receipt\x02" ‖ len ‖ request ‖ len ‖ result), each of request and result in its RFC 8785 canonical text (the result without its receipt member), each length 8 bytes big-endian. Whatever members the request and the result hold are sealed, the result's engine and schema among them. The first receipts (no canon member, $defs/first) sealed their writer's compact text under the domain ending \x01; they still verify. wai/extensions/quantum-providers.md section 8.2 states the seal in full, and section 8.4 what a verifier checks.

canon.description: The canonical form the digest is taken over.

digest.description: The digest signed, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

key.description: The signing key, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

signature.description: The signature, 64 bytes in lower-case hex.

time.description: When the receipt was issued and, where it states one, until when it is offered, by the signer's clock, in milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Absent on a receipt that seals no time (one from a host with no clock, or sealed before receipts stated one). With it, the digest is taken under the domain ending \x03 and ends with len ‖ the canonical text of this member, so the time cannot be changed or taken off (section 8.2).
